records.name: Uttar Pradesh
records.current_summary:
Uttar Pradesh hosts the most trans-visible public space in India: the Kinnar Akhara (trans/hijra monastic order) fielded a Mahamandaleshwar — one of its highest-ranking monks — at the head of 15 trans spiritual leaders in ceremonial bathing at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj (Jan-Feb 2025), the world's largest religious gathering, in a collaboration with the Naga Sadhus/Aghori grouping in the making since 2015. A trans visitor at the Kumbh is inside an institutionally recognised religious hierarchy, not a marginalised underground. The inclusion is contested, however: a rival leadership instalment drew protests from within the community and other sects, gurus threatened to boycott the 2037 Kumbh, and a top-ranking trans monk who objected was physically attacked on 12 February 2025. UP also has a constituted welfare board.

Against the national 0.43, UP sits +0.03. The Kinnar Akhara inclusion is visitor-facing, seasonal, and institutionally validated by the broader Akharas' governance structures, but the festival-week attack and boycott threats show the recognition is contested rather than settled. A further counterweight exists — a single transgender woman, Kajal, was strangled in Kanpur (Aug 2025) during a robbery — but this is a lone incident with no patterned state-actor response and does not constitute a regional finding under the single-incident rule. Compared to Tamil Nadu (0.53), UP lacks a comprehensive policy framework or judicial endorsement; compared to Maharashtra (0.38), UP does not show the festival-entry religion-screening that creates outing mechanisms at public gatherings. The net positive is narrow and temporally concentrated.

sources.claim: IPS (18 Feb 2025): at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj, Pavitra Nandagiri — a Mahamandaleshwar of the Kinnar Akhada, one of its highest-ranking monks — led 15 transgender spiritual leaders in the ceremonial bathing (fourth bath of the 45-day fair, 12 Feb 2025), marching with Naga Sadhus and Aghori. Documents UP's institutionalised trans religious hierarchy as the country's most trans-visible public space.

Trans Lives Matter TDoR record (10 Aug 2025): Kajal, 25, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, killed in a home-invasion robbery (suspect later arrested; her 12-year-old adopted brother also died). UP fatality logged in the 2025 TDoR list via local press (Bhaskar).

PIB / Ministry of Social Justice (8 Dec 2021): states must constitute Transgender Welfare Boards under s.10(1) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020; all state governments reminded 09 Oct 2020 to act. Framework for the record's welfare-board claim.

records.name: Chhattīsgarh
records.current_summary:
Chhattisgarh mirrors Maharashtra's garba screening: in Bastar district, VHP and Bajrang Dal members objected to non-Hindu sponsors and participants at garba events, claiming damage to "cultural purity," and pressed religion-gated entry conditions — tilak applied to participants, Hanuman Chalisa recitation before start, and a Varaha-avatar poster circulated to organisers — with at least three garba nights called off and tickets cancelled after written objections; police received a memorandum and arranged venue security. It is the same outing mechanism as in Maharashtra, minus the Aadhaar document checks: a religion-screened gate at a public festival examines and outs gender-nonconforming visitors via actors who are not supposed to be involved. Unlike Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh has no constituted transgender welfare board (absent from the 12-state/UT list). Additionally, in November 2024 a transgender woman, Kajal (alias "Coca Cola"), was stabbed to death and dumped in an abandoned quarry in Baloda Bazar district in a Rs 12 lakh contract killing over rival claims to a community leadership seat ("guru gaddi") — a single incident with no sourced second instance, recorded for pattern awareness rather than as a decisive factor.

Against the national 0.43, Chhattisgarh sits −0.06. The combination of festival-entrance screening (visitor-facing, seasonal, outing mechanism) and the absence of any state welfare apparatus distinguishes it from Maharashtra (0.38), which carries the same screening but at least has a board. Compared to Tripura (0.31), whose harm is state-police-driven border detention, Chhattisgarh's exposure is community-organiser-driven at private-adjacent festivals and the violence is a single unresolved incident. The gap to the national score is modest and confidence moderate.

sources.claim: Times of India (23 Sep 2025): in Bastar district, VHP and Bajrang Dal objected to non-Hindu sponsors of Navratri garba events and claimed the events had become platforms of 'obscenity and vulgarity'; participants admitted with a tilak. Supports the record's religious-conservatism framing.

Times of India, Raipur (22 Nov 2024): transgender woman Kajal, alias "Coca Cola", was lured out, stabbed and dumped in an abandoned quarry at village Dhabadih (Baloda Bazar) in a Rs 12 lakh contract killing orchestrated by a rival, Tapasya, to block her ascent to the Jora Math community head seat ("guru gaddi"); five suspects were arrested and Rs 10.5 lakh seized.

records.name: Ceara
records.current_summary:
Ceará is the most consistent lethal hotspot for trans and travesti people in Brazil's Northeast: 11 killings in 2024 — the region's highest toll and third nationally (G1, 28 January 2025, on the ANTRA dossier) — and 8 in 2025, tied with Minas Gerais for the highest state total of that year's 80 nationwide (Igbá Agência, 26 January 2026; SBT News). The 34% national drop is not read as improvement by ANTRA's leadership, since violence reappeared as attempted homicides (at least 75) (SBT News).

There is no state-level legal distinction: the federal constitution and penal code apply uniformly. What sets Ceará apart is sustained lethal exposure, and the national victim profile sharpens it for a visibly trans traveller — 97% of victims are travestis and trans women, over half aged 18–29, 70% of those with recorded race are Black, 97% killed in public spaces with most incidents outside capitals. Two consecutive years at the top of the ranking indicate an entrenched environment rather than a statistical blip.

Igbá Agência (26 Jan 2026): per the 9th ANTRA dossier, Ceará was among the states with most trans killings in 2025 with 8 cases; Brazil totalled 80 (18th year as world's highest). Among 57 victims with race data, 70% were Black (avg 77% over 2017-2025).

SBT News (26 Jan 2026): ANTRA 9th dossier — Ceará and Minas Gerais topped the 2025 state ranking with 8 killings each; Brazil's 80 total down 34% vs 2024, still 1st worldwide; 1,261 killings 2017-2025 (avg 140/yr).

records.name: Rio Granda do Norte
records.current_summary:
Rio Grande do Norte recorded zero trans killings in 2024 but jumped to 4 in 2025—the sharpest deterioration in the ANTRA dataset. Against a population of ~3.5 million, four cases yields approximately 1.14 killings per million per year, the highest per-capita rate among all 27 units in 2025 and roughly three times the national figure of ~0.38/million. The dossier cautions against reading a single-year zero as safety and notes the volatility.

This rate-driven exposure puts RN about 0.11 below the national 0.71. Compared with Ceará (0.61), RN's absolute count is lower (4 vs 8) but the per-capita risk is actually higher; the deviation from national is therefore slightly larger than one might expect from the raw numbers. The state sits within the Northeast bloc that accounted for 38 of 80 national killings in 2025.

No state-level statutory restriction or unique legal finding applies; the risk is purely a violence-rate signal. For a visitor, the small absolute numbers mean a single incident dramatically shifts perception, and the volatility suggests the environment can turn rapidly.

sources.claim: Sergipe em Debate report (27 Jan 2025) on the ANTRA dossier for 2024: 122 trans and travesti killings (16% down from 145 in 2023, close to the 125/year 2008-2024 average), five of them human-rights defenders, 95.9% of victims travestis/trans women, and systematic under-counting because official bodies do not record LGBTQIA+ victims properly — the dossier basis for Rio Grande do Norte appearing with zero recorded killings in 2024 before jumping to 4 in 2025.

SBT News report on the 9th ANTRA dossier (2025 data): Brazil 80 killings, 18th straight year topping the global tally; the state ranking places Ceará and Minas Gerais top with 8 each, while Paraíba and Rio Grande do Norte appear with 4 each — RN's jump from zero in 2024 makes it the sharpest deterioration in the dataset; the Northeast recorded 38 of the 80 killings.

sources.title: Mulher trans é assassinada dentro de casa em Mossoró; cinco são suspeitos
sources.claim: Saiba Mais (RN) reports that in the early hours of 4 May 2026 a 27-year-old transgender woman, Emanuelle Samira Fernandes Neta, was shot dead inside her rented home on Rua Vivaldo Dantas in the Dom Jaime Câmara neighbourhood of Mossoró, western Rio Grande do Norte, after five men broke in and executed her while she slept; military police found the body on a routine patrol, and one suspect was arrested with a pistol and booked for illegal firearms discharge and armed criminal association. RN trans-rights group ATTRANSPARÊNCIA/RN publicly mourned Samira as an artist killed by the transphobia she faced. The case documents lethal violence against trans women in Rio Grande do Norte continuing after the years this record covers, matching the record's warning that a single-year zero should not be read as safety.

sources.title: Mulher trans é encontrada morta dentro de casa na Praia da Pipa; Civil investiga o caso
sources.claim: Saiba Mais (RN) reports that a transgender woman known as Naomi was found dead inside her own home in Praia da Pipa, Tibau do Sul municipality on the southern coast of Rio Grande do Norte, killed by stab wounds in late February 2026, with the Civil Police opening an investigation and RN trans-rights association ATTRANSPARÊNCIA/RN calling for justice. The same article reproduces the ANTRA 2025 dossier figures: 80 trans killings in Brazil in 2025 (a 34% drop from 2024), 38 of them in the Nordeste, and zero registered trans killings in Rio Grande do Norte in 2025 — a count that conflicts with this record's stated 4 killings for the state in 2025 and needs reconciliation in rework.

records.name: Paraiba
records.current_summary:
Paraíba recorded 4 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025 — mid-pack in the ANTRA dossier's state ranking, alongside Paraná, Rio Grande do Norte and São Paulo — within a national total of 80 that still leads the world for the 16th consecutive year (SBT News, 26 January 2026; CNN Brasil). No Paraíba-specific statute, ordinance or enforcement policy affecting trans people was found in the audited sources; the federal framework applies uniformly.

The documented signal is therefore exposure, not law: the dossiers' consistent victim profile — young, Black, poor and Northeastern, 97% travestis and trans women, most killings in public spaces at night and outside state capitals, frequently mis-recorded by authorities — concentrates risk on people who present visibly in public. The state's absolute count doubled the best-recorded small-state figure of the same table's lower rows, and sits inside the region the dossiers identify as Brazil's hardest-hit.

sources.claim: SBT News (26 Jan 2026): ANTRA 2025 dossier — Paraíba recorded 4 trans killings in 2025, mid-pack (tied with Paraná, Rio Grande do Norte, São Paulo); Brazil total 80. Supports the record's state tally.

CNN Brasil (2024 dossier): Paraíba recorded 5 trans killings in 2024; Rio Grande do Norte, Acre and Roraima zero; Bahia, Mato Grosso and Pernambuco 8 each. Earlier-year comparison for the record's mid-pack framing.

records.name: Minas Gerais
records.current_summary:
Minas Gerais ranked 2nd nationally in 2024 with 12 killings and tied for the top in 2025 with 8 (matching Ceará). Against a population of ~21 million, the 2025 rate of ~0.38/million sits at the national average, but the consistency of appearing in the top two every year signals a structurally elevated environment compared with states that fluctuate. The 2024 total of 12 placed it behind only São Paulo.

These factors put Minas Gerais about 0.07 below the national 0.71. Compared with Ceará (0.61), which matched the same 2025 absolute count on a much smaller population, Minas Gerais' per-capita exposure is roughly half—so the deviation is more moderate. Compared with São Paulo (no deviation recorded), which led the 2024 count at 16 but fell sharply in 2025, Minas Gerais' consistency across both years is the distinguishing risk factor.

No state-specific legal restriction or unique ordinance was identified. The risk for a visitor is violence-exposure, patterned over two years, in a large interior state where the 68%-outside-capitals finding of the 2024 dossier implies added danger away from Belo Horizonte.

sources.claim: Sergipe em Debate / ANTRA 2024 dossier (27 Jan 2025): Minas Gerais ranked 2nd nationally with 12 trans killings in 2024 (São Paulo 16, Ceará 11); 2017-2024 cumulative MG 100. Supports the record's 2024 ranking.
SBT News (26 Jan 2026): ANTRA 2025 dossier — Minas Gerais tied 1st with Ceará at 8 trans killings in 2025; national total 80. Supports the record's 2025 tie figure.

records.name: Pernambuco
records.current_summary:
Pernambuco recorded 7 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, behind only the two 8-count states in the ANTRA dossier's ranking of that year's 80 national killings (SBT News, 26 January 2026; Valor Internacional). No Pernambuco-specific legal restriction or ordinance was identified in the audited sources; the federal framework applies uniformly.

The dossiers add a geographic caution that cuts against capital-centred assumptions: roughly two-thirds of such killings in Brazil happen in interior cities rather than state capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policy are weaker (SBT News). A visibly trans visitor in Pernambuco's mid-sized and interior municipalities is therefore in the geography where the recorded danger actually concentrates — alongside a victim profile of young (majority 18–29), overwhelmingly Black (70% of those recorded) travestis and trans women.

sources.claim: SBT News (26 Jan 2026): ANTRA 2025 dossier — Pernambuco recorded 7 trans killings in 2025, behind only the 8-count states (Ceará, Minas Gerais); Brazil total 80. Supports the record's tally.

sources.title: Pernambuco foi o segundo estado que mais matou pessoas trans e travestis em 2025, diz estudo
sources.claim: Diario de Pernambuco, Jan. 27, 2026: Pernambuco was the second Brazilian state with the most killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, with 7 homicides, per the ANTRA dossier released on Jan. 26 — the state's lowest annual count since 2022 (13), after 9 in 2023 and 8 in 2024. The dossier counts 80 trans people killed nationally in 2025, 349 killings across the Northeast from 2017 to 2025, and 83 violent deaths of trans people in Pernambuco over six years, 6th-most in the national ranking for that period. For this record: a Pernambuco-specific confirmation of the state's 2025 total and a year-by-year series showing its repeated high ranking.

sources.title: Mulher trans é morta a tiros em Belo Jardim
sources.claim: G1 Caruaru e Região, Oct. 3, 2025: a trans woman was shot dead inside her home on Oct. 2, 2025 in Belo Jardim, in the Agreste interior of Pernambuco, and the Civil Police opened an inquiry to identify the author and motive, with no arrests reported at publication. The report recalls the national ANTRA count of 122 trans people killed in Brazil in 2024. For this record: a documented 2025 killing outside the Recife capital region, consistent with the dossier finding that most such killings occur in interior municipalities.

sources.title: Morte de transexual negra é registrada no Agreste de Pernambuco; mais um caso preocupa ativistas
sources.claim: Alma Preta, July 7, 2021: Fabiana da Silva Lucas, a 30-year-old Black trans woman, was found dead on the morning of that day along highway PE-160 in Santa Cruz do Capibaribe, in the Agreste of Pernambuco, killed by several knife strikes; it was the state's third recorded case of killed trans or travesti people that month. Pernambuco's Civil Police told press the suspect, a 22-year-old known as 'Gaúcho', was lynched by locals at the scene. For this record: a documented interior-state killing of a Black travesti matching the victim profile and geography described in the summary.

records.name: Bahia
records.current_summary:
Bahia recorded 7 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025 — among the highest state tallies of that year's 80, on the largest population among the upper-ranked states (SBT News, 26 January 2026; Valor Internacional). No Bahia-specific ordinance or statutory restriction was identified; federal law applies uniformly across Brazil.

The documented picture is a high absolute toll diluted by size rather than eliminated by it: the dossiers place the state inside the Northeastern region that accounts for the bulk of national killings, with the consistent victim profile (97% travestis and trans women, majority aged 18–29, 70% Black among racially identified cases, most killings outside state capitals) describing who carries the risk. For a visibly trans visitor the operative fact is persistence — Bahia appears in the top ranked band of consecutive annual dossiers — not any local legal regime.
records.current_outOfScope: The state contains indigenous territories with parallel community authority, but no sourced trans-specific jurisdiction was found in them; general land-governance arrangements there do not change trans visitor risk.

sources.claim: SBT News (26 Jan 2026): ANTRA 2025 dossier — Bahia recorded 7 trans killings in 2025, second tier behind the 8-count states; among 1,261 killings 2017-2025 Bahia is 3rd with 97 (São Paulo 151, Ceará 107). Supports the record's tally.

sources.title: Morte de mulher trans na Bahia é investigada como feminicídio; suspeito deixou corpo em delegacia e foi liberado
sources.claim: G1 Bahia, Dec. 9, 2025: police are investigating as feminicide the killing of Rhianna, an 18-year-old trans woman, choked to death in Luís Eduardo Magalhães, in the west of Bahia, on the weekend of Dec. 6-7. The suspect, a 19-year-old app driver, drove the victim's body to the police station himself and was released after confessing and claiming self-defence; the Civil Police confirmed the feminicide investigation. For this record: a documented killing in Bahia framed by the state police as gender-based (feminicide) with the suspect initially released.

sources.title: Bahia é o sétimo estado que mais mata trans, aponta relatório; relembre casos
sources.claim: G1 Bahia, Jan. 27, 2023: the ANTRA dossier ranked Bahia the seventh Brazilian state most killing trans people, with 7 killings of travestis in the state in 2022, and recapped emblematic cases; Pernambuco led that year's negative ranking nationally. For this record: documents Bahia's appearance in the top-ranked band of consecutive annual dossiers, grounding the summary's persistence finding across years.
